questions.question: One end of a spring of natural length h and spring constant k is fixed at the ground, and the other end is fitted with a smooth ring of mass m that is allowed to slide on a horizontal rod fixed at height h as shown in the figure. Initially, the spring makes an angle of 37^{} with the vertical when the system is released from rest. Find the speed of the ring when the spring becomes vertical.
questions.explanation: Initially the spring length is L_i=h/37^=5h/4 , so its extension is h/4 . When vertical, its length is h , equal to natural length. Energy conservation gives 12k(h/4)²=12mv² , so v= h4√(k/m) . Hence (C).

questions.question: A spring of spring constant k=50 {Nm}^{-1} is compressed to 2 {~m} by a block of mass 1 {~kg} as shown in the figure. If the spring-block system is set free at this position, then find the value of x where the velocity of the block becomes zero. (Take =0.5 )
questions.explanation: Initial spring energy is 12k(2)²=100\,{J} . Friction is mg=0.5(1)(10)=5\,{N} . If the block stops after extending the spring by x , energy balance gives 100=5(2+x)+12(50)x² . Thus 25x²+5x-90=0 x=1.8\,{m} .

questions.question: Find the speed of the 5 {~kg} block by using the work-energy theorem if the 5 {~kg} block slides down by 2 {~m} when the system is set free as shown in the figure.
questions.explanation: Firstly, let us find the relation between the blocks using the constraint relationship. On finding the values of velocities at the six points and adding them, we get the following: vA + vB + vC + vD + vE + vF = 0 ⇒ 0 – v' – v' + 0 + 0 + v = 0 ⇒ 2v' = v ⇒v'=v2 So, when the 5 kg block moves by 2 m, the 2 kg block will move by 1 m. The only work done is due to the gravitational force. WDG = m1g × l1 – m2g × l2 ⇒ WDG = 50 × 2 – 20 × 1 ⇒ WDG = 80 J By applying the work-energy theorem, we get the following: ⇒WDG=Kf−Ki ⇒WDG=12×5×v²×12×2×v22−0 ⇒80=5v²2+v²4 ⇒80=11v²4 ⇒v=28011ms−1

questions.question: Find the speed of the blocks by using the work- energy theorem if they move by 2 m after they are released.
questions.explanation: The 2\,{kg} mass descends 2\,{m} , losing potential energy mgh=(2)(10)(2)=40\,{J} . This becomes kinetic energy of both masses: 40=12(1+2)v² . Hence v²=80/3 v=√(80/3)\,{m s}^{-1} . Thus (D).

questions.question: A ring of mass 2 {~kg} can slide over a smooth vertical pole. A light string is attached to the ring passing over a smooth fixed pulley at a distance of 4 {~m} from the pole as shown in Fig. At the other end of the string block of mass 1 {~kg} is attached, lying over a smooth fixed wedge. Find the speed of 1 {~kg} block when the ring falls by 3 {~m} . The wedge and the pole are fixed. (Take g = 10 m/s2)
questions.explanation: Let the speed of the 2 kg ring be v when it has fallen by 3 m. The speed of the 1 kg block will also be v due to the string constraint. The potential energy lost by the ring is given by: ΔUring =mring ·g·h The potential energy gained by the block is given by: ΔUblock =mblock ·g·hblock The kinetic energy of the system is given by: K=12mring v²+12mblock v²Using conservation of energy: ΔUring -ΔUblock =K

hi.question: 2 kg द्रव्यमान की एक वलय एक चिकने ऊर्ध्वाधर खंभे पर सरक सकती है। खंभे से 4 m की दूरी पर एक चिकनी स्थिर घिरनी से गुजरती हुई एक हल्की डोरी वलय से जुड़ी हुई है, जैसा कि चित्र में दिखाया गया है। डोरी के दूसरे सिरे पर 1 kg द्रव्यमान का एक गुटका जुड़ा हुआ है, जो एक चिकने स्थिर वेज पर रखा है। 1 kg गुटके की गति ज्ञात कीजिए जब वलय 3 m नीचे गिरती है। वेज और खंभा स्थिर हैं। (g = 10 m/s2 लीजिए)
hi.explanation: मान लीजिए कि 2 kg के वलय की चाल v है जब वह 3 m नीचे गिर चुका होता है। डोरी के अवरोध के कारण 1 kg के गुटके की चाल भी v ही होगी। वलय द्वारा खोई गई स्थितिज ऊर्जा निम्न द्वारा दी जाती है: ΔUवलय ​= mवलय⋅g⋅h गुटके द्वारा प्राप्त स्थितिज ऊर्जा निम्न द्वारा दी जाती है: ΔUगुटके ​= mगुटके ​⋅g⋅hगुटके निकाय की गतिज ऊर्जा निम्न द्वारा दी जाती है: K=12mवलय ​v²+12mगुटकेv² ऊर्जा संरक्षण का उपयोग करने पर: ΔUवलय​ − ΔUगुटके = K
